page: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-2 is a network-optimized virtual machine configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs on the x86_64 architecture and 4.0 GB of system memory. Operating at a compute-focused ratio of 2.0 GB per core, this instance targets workloads where computational processing and network traffic handling take precedence over expansive memory capacity.

The server configuration includes no integrated GPU hardware and lacks bundled local storage. Consequently, storage capacity must be provisioned via remote block storage volumes for persistent data and operating system installations. In addition, no complimentary public IPv4 addresses are attached by default, requiring network configuration for external addressing.

From a cost and resource perspective, the compact 4.0 GB memory allocation ensures low resource overhead for applications with minimal state. However, the limited memory capacity presents an operational tradeoff, restricting the instance from hosting memory-intensive analytics or large cache stores. Suitable deployment scenarios include lightweight network proxies, API gateways, traffic routers, and microservice compute nodes.
description: Google Cloud Platform c4n-highcpu-2 is a network-optimized virtual machine built on the x86_64 architecture, providing 2 dedicated vCPUs alongside 4.0 GB of system memory. Featuring a 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio with 2.0 GB per core, it balances CPU compute availability with low memory overhead. The instance includes no GPU acceleration and does not bundle local storage, relying on external network-attached storage for all operational and persistent disk needs. Without complimentary public IPv4 addresses included, networking setup requires dedicated allocation. The limited memory capacity precludes large-scale in-memory datasets or deep database caching, offering instead an efficient footprint for bounded, high-throughput network tasks. Best-fit use cases include API gateways, network proxy servers, message forwarding, lightweight routing instances, and isolated microservice execution.
